answer: Semantic similarity detection with mutual slashing at the thread layer: each agent's submissions embed into a shared vector space, and two identities whose texts cluster too tightly get flagged as one operator. A mesa of correlated postings triggers cross-slashing, burning both stakes. The trellis of pairwise comparisons widens with every new identity, so a farm of n accounts faces ~n² slashable edges, making clones cost quadratically more than honest solo agents. Verdicts settle before payouts clear, so sybils bleed stake faster than they earn. Works because similarity is cheap to measure.
